newsitem.title: TAIWAN: S.Korea nudges bitter Taiwan to restore air links.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea nudges bitter Taiwan to restore air links.

text.p: A visiting South Korean delegation on Friday called on Taiwan to restore air links cut in 1992 when Seoul shocked Taipei by switching diplomatic ties to Beijing.

The Foreign Ministry said Chung Jey-moon, a senior parliament deputy from the ruling New Korea Party, was in Taiwan to press President Lee Teng-hui and other officials to end its ban on aviation ties, but played down the visit.
"This is merely a friendly tour by South Korean lawmakers," a ministry spokesman said by telephone. "They have expressed a desire to push for an earlier discussion on aviation links."
Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang was cautious and said there was no timetable for resuming air links.

"Relations need to be promoted step by step with patience and wisdom," Chang said on state radio after meeting Chung and his delegation. "I can feel the sincerity of the South Korean government, but both sides need more time to resolve their problems."

The unofficial talks, expected also to touch on Taiwan's stalled bid to enter the World Trade Organisation, would help rebuild "mutual trust" and cooperation between the governments, a ministry statement said.
Chung said Seoul coveted better ties.
"We want to strengthen friendly relations between people of the two countries and to boost cooperation between the two governments," Chung told the China Times in an interview.
"Friendly bilateral ties were severed but such relations should and will definitely be restored," Chung was quoted as saying. "We need friendship with both Taipei and Beijing."
Chung, whose delegation arrived on Thursday for a four-day visit, said flights should resume as soon as possible and said their suspension was "inconvienent and unnecessary".

Taipei angrily suspended air links and a range of other trade privileges with Seoul in 1992 after its biggest Asian ally ended four decades of anti-communist solidarity and dropped recognition of Taiwan's exiled Republic of China in favour of ties with mainland China.
Beijing has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province not entitled to sovereign ties since the Chinese civil war separated them in 1949.
South Korea, backed by the United States and Taiwan, went to war with China from 1950 to 1953 to counter the spread of communism in the northern half of the Korean peninsula.
The visiting South Koreans, in their meeting with President Lee, expressed Seoul's strong desire to improve relations with Taiwan, the state-funded Central News Agency said.
Chung said his government supports Taiwan's membership bid in the World Trade Organisation.

Taiwan agreed last week to lift a ban on Korean car imports dating to 1992. Taiwan will take 7,000 units in 1996 under a quota that calls for 10 percent yearly increase. The quota jumps to 10,000 after Taiwan joins the WTO with 20 percent annual rises thereafter.
